steps.title: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
steps.body: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, near Avignon, was named after the 14th century popes' summer castle. It allows 13 grape varieties, but Grenache usually leads, often 70% or more. Its famous galets roulés, large round stones, store heat and reflect light. In 1923, Baron Le Roy's rules there helped inspire France's AOC system.

steps.title: The southern Rhône
steps.body: Gigondas and Vacqueyras, nearby, make powerful Grenache-led reds. Côtes du Rhône and Côtes du Rhône Villages offer more affordable versions. Château Rayas is a famous Châteauneuf made almost entirely from Grenache, on sandy soil, showing the grape's elegance.

steps.prompt: What are the galets roulés of Châteauneuf-du-Pape?
options: Large round stones that store heat
steps.explanation: These river stones store heat by day and release it at night.

steps.title: Rosé
steps.body: Grenache is the main grape of many rosés: Provence, Tavel and Navarra's rosado. Its thin skins give pale colour quickly, and its red fruit and body suit dry rosé. Tavel, in the southern Rhône, is a rosé-only appellation, fuller and darker than Provence.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Châteauneuf-du-Pape is Grenache-led, with galets and 13 grapes
